parameters.content:
## IT Helpdesk Automation Workflow

Starter template from agentmelt.com — configure before running:

1. Fill in "Config (edit me)" (name, approver, quiet hours; test_mode stays on for the first week).
2. Add credentials to every service node (Anthropic, mail, CRM, database…).
3. Replace placeholder URLs, queries and field mappings with yours.
4. Set the trigger: Messages to the IT bot or #it-help channel, and new tickets in Jira Service Management, Freshservice or ServiceNow.
5. Keep the gates: 'Needs a person?' after every AI step, 'Approved?' after the approval — wire their dead ends to a sheet or a channel.
6. Keep the guardrails:
   - Identity is taken from the chat platform's SSO, never from the message; sensitive actions require a fresh MFA step.
   - Access grants always require manager (or app owner) approval recorded in the ticket; privileged groups are excluded from self-service.
   - Every automated action is logged with requester, approver and timestamp for audit.
   - Outage reports and security concerns bypass the bot and go straight to the on-call engineer.

Full blueprint and pricing: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/it-helpdesk-automation/
Want it built and run for you? $297/month · custom $5,000–9,000 one-time

nodes.name: Webhook: Receive the request
nodes.notes:
Receive the request

Message text, requester identity (verified through the chat platform's SSO), device and location from the MDM where available.

assignments.name: config.your_name
assignments.value: Your name — signs every outgoing message

assignments.name: config.approver
assignments.value: #approvals — a Slack channel, or an email address

nodes.name: Config (edit me)
nodes.notes:
Fill these in once; every later node reads them as $('Config (edit me)').item.json.config.*

test_mode = true: log what the workflow would write, without writing it, for the first week.
approval_mode = true: the approval node waits for a person; switch off per message type once it has earned it.

Also point the nodes at your own sources:
- Slack / Teams (identity-verified requests)
- IT knowledge base (Confluence, Notion, help centre)
- Identity provider (Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace)
- MDM and licence platforms (Jamf, Intune, licence manager)
- Help desk (Jira SM, Freshservice, ServiceNow)

nodes.name: Text Classifier: Classify the request
nodes.notes:
Classify the request

Password/MFA, access request, software/licence, hardware, how-to, outage report, other — with urgency. Outage reports skip to incident handling.

nodes.name: Needs a person?
nodes.notes: True = the AI step was not sure or flagged the item → dead letter, a person looks. False = continue. Wire the dead letter to a Slack message or a sheet so nothing fails silently.

nodes.name: Needs a person: Classify the request
nodes.notes: Dead letter. Replace this no-op with a Slack message or a sheet row that carries the raw item and the reason — silent failures are the ones that cost.

options.systemMessage:
You are the "Answer from the knowledge base" step of the IT Helpdesk Automation Workflow workflow run by Agentmelt.
Task: How-to questions are answered from the IT knowledge base with the steps and a link; the agent asks a clarifying question when the request is ambiguous.

Rules:
- Identity is taken from the chat platform's SSO, never from the message; sensitive actions require a fresh MFA step.
- Access grants always require manager (or app owner) approval recorded in the ticket; privileged groups are excluded from self-service.
- Every automated action is logged with requester, approver and timestamp for audit.
- Outage reports and security concerns bypass the bot and go straight to the on-call engineer.
- Answer only from the data provided in the input. If something is missing, say so in the output instead of guessing.
- If this step produces a message or a document, put the full text in `draft` (and a `subject` if it is an email); put a one-line summary in `summary`.
- Set `needs_human` true whenever you are unsure, the input is unusual, or a rule above applies; a person will look at it.
- Return valid JSON matching the output schema; no prose outside the JSON.

nodes.name: Switch: Self-service actions with approval
nodes.notes:
Self-service actions with approval

Password reset → identity-provider API after MFA verification. Access to a group or app → manager approval request in Slack, then the identity-provider call. Software → licence check, then MDM deployment or a purchase request. Hardware → ticket with the asset details.

parameters.notes: Okta/Entra ID/Google Workspace for identity actions, Jamf/Intune for software deployment, the licence platform for seat assignment — each call logged with requester, approver and timestamp.

Okta/Entra ID/Google Workspace for identity actions, Jamf/Intune for software deployment, the licence platform for seat assignment — each call logged with requester, approver and timestamp.

nodes.name: Jira: Create or update the ticket
nodes.notes:
Create or update the ticket

Every request, resolved or not, becomes a ticket with the classification, the actions taken and the conversation, so metrics and audits are complete.

nodes.name: Slack: Route unresolved requests
nodes.notes:
Route unresolved requests

Anything the bot cannot resolve is assigned to the right IT queue with the context and a summary; the requester is told who has it and the expected time.

nodes.name: Schedule Trigger: Improve the knowledge base
nodes.notes:
Improve the knowledge base

Weekly: questions the agent could not answer, grouped by topic, become draft KB articles for IT to approve; resolved-by-bot rate and time-to-resolve reported per category.
